claims.claim: Arena ships a full-screen terminal UI (TUI) that is an interactive hub for running scenarios, browsing past results and chatting with an agent.
Running promptarena with no subcommand from any directory opens the hub.
The hub opens in the alternate screen.
On startup the hub looks for an Arena config in the working directory, for example config.arena.yaml, and loads it if found.
No config is required to launch the hub.
Pages that need a config (Run, Chat, Inspect) stay disabled until a config is present.
Results default to the out/ directory beside the config.
The hub menu shows five entries: View, Run, Chat, Inspect and Deploy, with the loaded config shown above them.
The hub menu has five entries.
The Run entry runs scenarios against providers.
The View entry browses past test results.
The Chat entry opens an interactive multi-turn session.
The Inspect entry explores config and state.
The Deploy entry walks through preflight, plan, confirm, apply and status.
The Up and Down arrow keys move the menu selection.
The Enter key opens the highlighted page.
The Esc key goes back one page and pops the navigation stack.
The q key quits only at the root menu, and inside a page it does not quit.
Ctrl-C quits from anywhere in the hub.
The View page is always available because it only needs a results directory.
Opening Run, Chat or Inspect without a loaded config shows a notice explaining why.
The Deploy page requires the loaded config to have a deploy: section.
Switching the active config from within the hub rebuilds the engine so the new config takes effect immediately.
The Inspect page shows the resolved config and live state, including providers, agents, scenarios and workflow or memory state.
The Inspect screenshot lists prompt configs, scenarios with task and turn counts, three registered providers with models and files, and declared tools.
The promptarena view subcommand exists.
promptarena view with no argument browses the current directory.
promptarena view out/ browses a specific results directory.
view opens a file browser over past JSON result files.
Selecting a run in view previews its metadata.
view lets you drill into the full conversation transcript for any completed test.
The view directory argument is optional and defaults to the current directory.
view errors out when the given path does not exist or is not a directory.
view deep-links with the results page as the root of the navigation stack.
In view, Esc or q exits the program rather than returning to the hub menu.
The results browser screenshot shows a numbered turn list with alternating user and assistant roles.
The promptarena chat subcommand exists.
promptarena chat with no flags uses config.arena.yaml.
promptarena chat --config config.arena.yaml sets the config path explicitly.
Typing a message and pressing Enter sends it, and the agent replies turn by turn.
The chat session keeps conversation state between turns.
The -v and --verbose flags are available on chat.
With verbose enabled, chat tees raw provider events and transcription to promptarena.log.
The chat page is the navigation stack root, so Esc exits back to the shell; q exits only when the input box is not focused (a focused input receives q as text).
chat opens on a provider picker.
The provider picker reads digit keys as selections.
The chat screenshot shows a get_order_status tool call and its result, with token and cost totals.
The --voice flag starts a hands-free voice conversation with chat.
Voice mode requires PortAudio installed on the host.
PortAudio is loaded on demand only when a voice session starts.
promptarena chat --voice --config config.arena.yaml is a valid command.
In voice mode the agent responds with synthesized audio.
If PortAudio is missing, the command prints an install hint and only voice is unavailable.
The run command shows a live progress TUI by default.
promptarena run --config config.arena.yaml is a valid command.
The live run view shows a live feed of runs, a log panel and results as they complete.
The live run view updates in place until every combination finishes.
The run screenshot shows an Active Runs table with provider, status, scenario, region and duration columns, and a log panel streaming turn and provider-call events.
The --ci flag turns the live TUI off and falls back to plain streaming logs.
--simple is an alias of --ci.
promptarena run --ci --config config.arena.yaml is a valid command.
In --ci mode Arena exits with a non-zero exit code when any run errors.
In --ci mode Arena exits with a non-zero exit code when any assertion fails.
The Deploy wizard walks through the same deploy lifecycle as promptarena deploy on the CLI.
The Deploy page is enabled once the loaded config has a deploy: section.
Deploy is the fifth entry on the hub menu, below Inspect.
Deploy is selectable only when the loaded config has a deploy: section.
Opening Deploy starts on a readiness gate before anything is planned or applied.
The Preflight page shows the target provider and the environment name.
The environment name is shown prominently in preflight.
Preflight shows an adapter presence line as a check mark with the provider and version when the adapter is installed.
Preflight shows the text not installed with a cross mark when the adapter is missing.
Preflight shows an Auth check mark or cross mark depending on whether the adapter has a valid token.
If the adapter is not installed, preflight blocks further steps.
Preflight prints the command promptarena deploy adapter install <provider> when the adapter is missing.
Installing, listing and removing adapters is CLI-only in v1.
The TUI detects the gap and points at the CLI rather than installing an adapter itself.
When the adapter supports login and you are not authenticated, preflight offers a Login step.
The Login step is triggered with the l key.
The in-TUI login runs the same loopback OAuth flow as promptarena deploy login.
The login flow writes the config and token for you.
Pressing p renders the plan as a colored diff.
The space key expands the collapsed no change section on the plan page.
The a key accepts the plan and moves to Confirm.
Drifted resources are badged with a warning sign and N drifted.
The plan diff uses the same plus, tilde, minus and exclamation vocabulary as the CLI plan output.
The plan screenshot shows a summary of 0 to create, 2 to update and 0 to delete.
The plan screenshot shows two adapter warnings.
Resources already matching the config are hidden by default on the plan page.
The space key toggles the hidden no-change resources into the list.
In the default environment, Confirm shows a y or N prompt.
In any non-default environment, including production, you must type the environment name exactly to proceed.
The y key confirms the apply in Deploy.
Deploy acquires a deploy lock before it applies.
Apply shows live resource progress and logs in the TUI.
Pressing s checks status after apply or on its own.
Status shows a check mark for healthy, a cross mark for unhealthy and a question mark for unknown.
destroy, import, refresh and adapter install, list and remove are not part of the Deploy wizard in v1.
Pressing Ctrl-C starts a 5-second watchdog and prints a hint.
Pressing Ctrl-C a second time, or waiting out the 5 seconds, force-exits Arena.
The force exit restores the cursor, the primary screen buffer and terminal attributes.
The hub's Run page writes the report formats run would write with no flags to the output directory resolved against the config's directory when its runs finish.
